tossups.text: One class of antagonists of this compound's receptor is used to treat the nausea associated with chemotherapy, and carcinoid syndrome occurs when tumors secrete this compound excessively. In the hepatic portal vein, platelets commonly sequester this compound. This compound's production is dependent on TPH1 in the pineal gland and TPH2 in the Raphe nuclei. LSD agonizes this compound's 2A receptor, and this compound is most abundantly produced in the enterochromaffin cells of the GI tract. It breaks down into 5-HIAA in the liver via monoamine oxidases, and this neurotransmitter's effects can be enhanced by Celexa and Zoloft, which block this compounds reuptake. Synthesized from tryptophan and also known as 5-HT, for 10 points, name this neurotransmitter whose levels are lowered in depression and anxiety disorders.

Three of these words in Mandarin, all pronounced "tā," sound the same when spoken but appear different when written. In French, "vous" (voo) serves as a formal word of this type, as opposed to "tu" (too). These are the only words in English that have different forms for the subject and object of sentences, and their second-person variety is the same in the singular and the plural. For 10 points, what substitutes for nouns include "they" and "me"?

This poet's complaint about Ben Jonson's phrase "the bodies that those souls were frighted from" is probably the source of the prescription against using prepositions to end sentences with. Matthew Prior and Charles Montagu parodied one of this author's poems using the story of the country mouse and the city mouse. That poem, which coined the term "blaze of glory," begins by describing an animal "immortal and unchang'd." This poet was targeted in the satire The Medal of John Bayes by a Protestant poet who he described as "the last great prophet of tautology." A poem by this author notes "when fate summons, monarchs must obey" after starting "all human things are subject to decay," and satirizes Thomas Shadwell. For 10 points, name this poet of The Hind and the Panther and Mac Flecknoe.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for lung volumes and capacities. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this diaphragm-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The diaphragm is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in lung volumes and capacities.

tossups.text: This author's only novel describes its titular character as "wonderfully handsome, with his finely curved scarlet lips, his frank blue eyes, and his crisp gold hair". That titular character's life is transformed after meeting Lord Henry Wotton, a friend of Basil Hallward. This author is perhaps better known for his poetry, such as The Ballad of Reading Gaol, and his plays, including A Woman of No Importance and Salome. For 10 points, identify this Irish playwright and author of Lady Windemere's Fan, The Importance of Being Ernest, and The Picture of Dorian Gray.

Gilgamesh has a dream in which he embraces one of these objects that falls from the sky. In the story of Bricrui's Feast, Cuchulainn proves he deserves the champion's portion of the meal by standing up to a giant wielding one of these weapons. Because his grandfather Aleus hides his arms, Ancaeus is forced to face the Caledonian Boar wielding only the labrys, a type of this weapon. One of these weapons is used to kill twenty-one generations of Kshatriyas and to sever Ganesh's broken tusk. That example is wielded by the sixth avatar of Vishnu. In the Odyssey, twelve of them are lined up so that Odysseus can shoot an arrow through their handles. Hephaestus uses either a rock or one of these weapons to split Zeus's head during the birth of Athena. For 10 points, name this weapon which is used by Paul Bunyan to chop down trees.

One book by this thinker contains a chapter on "The Perverse Implantation" that appears in a larger section rejecting the "repressive hypothesis." This thinker argued that epistemes are the foundation of epistemology in his The Archaeology of Knowledge. In one book, this thinker analyzed the gradual ostracism of undesirables as a "Great Confinement," while in another book he examined the torture of Robert-François Damiens and the "unequal gaze" of Jeremy Bentham's Panopticon as part of the evolution of the prison system. For 10 points, name this 20th century French thinker who wrote Madness and Civilization as well as Discipline and Punish.

This author's friend Joseph Mitchell inherited his library after his death, and was disgusted to learn that he used strips of fried bacon as bookmarks. A memoir of Paris by this writer observes that having enough money on hand "for three days" is the "optimal financial situation" for the "serious apprentice eater". This man claimed that some of the worst reporting of his time occurred during the coverage of Elizabeth Bentley in his book Of Mink and Red Herring. His later works include profiles of Huey Long's brother. This author of the memoir Between Meals wrote a piece calling a man nicknamed Hurricane Jackson a "nanimal." A comparison of Rocky Marciano to the whale Moby Dick appears in this author's piece "Ahab and Nemesis", one of his essays about a discipline of "bruising". For 10 points, name this longtime editor of The New Yorker whose essays on boxing are found in The Sweet Science.

Sodium iodide scintillators are often used to counter the appearance of false peaks in gamma ray spectra , which is called this phenomenon's namesake edge. At higher frequency, its differential cross section is calculable by the Klein-Nishina formula. Planck's constant divided by rest mass times speed of light gives the wavelength named for this effect. That wavelength is multiplied by 1 minus cosine of the angle of scattered photons to give the shift in wavelength following this type of scattering. For 10 points, name this phenomenon, a photon's decrease in wavelength and increase in energy when it collides with an electron, named after an American physicist.

This artist painted a series of "Cloud Studies" during his "skying" sessions in which he painted en plein air. This artist depicted a beached shipwreck in The Chain Pier. At the 1824 Salon, Charles X [the tenth] awarded the gold medal to a painting by this artist that depicts a partially concealed man in a canoe. One of this painter's "six-footers" depicts a view of Dedham village. An iconic painting by this artist depicts horses pulling a large wagon across a river next to Willy Lott's cottage. This artist painted many depictions of Salisbury Cathedral. For 10 points, name this English landscape artist of The Hay Wain.

This natural phenomenon can be graphed by sinusoidal [sye-nuh-soy-dull] functions. This phenomenon's standing type has minimal displacement at its nodes. Compton scattering demonstrates that light behaves like a particle, and not just as this phenomenon. For 10 points, name this physical phenomenon that can carry energy without transferring mass, as seen on the moving surface of the ocean.

Anthony Giddens argues that performing this practice in the afternoon declined due to an acknowledgment that it was distinct from the "progressive deprivation of rights." A recent book by David Garland analyzes the persistence of this practice after a series of Supreme Court cases in the 1970s that assessed "weighing" and "non-weighing" approaches to it. A book opens with a description of how this practice was applied to Robert-François Damiens ("dahm-YEN"), and argues that disorder of its public form led to a push to privatize the use of "sovereign power." Gregg v. Georgia outlined the procedures that state courts must follow in order for this practice not to violate the Eighth Amendment, ending a moratorium on it established by Furman v. Georgia. For 10 points, name this punishment normally carried out in the United States through lethal injection.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for autonomic nervous system. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cranial nerve-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cranial nerve is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in autonomic nervous system.

tossups.text: Named answer required This speech denounces the threat of nationwide oligarchy by citing Thor's struggle to lift the Midgard-serpent disguised as a cat in the hall of Utgard-Loki. The "temple of constitutional liberty" is said to be "grander than the Ephesian dome" according to this speech, which also calls the ballot-box "more precious than ivory and marble." In this speech, a senator is compared to Don Quixote, who considered Dulcinea "chaste in his sight, though polluted in the eyes of the world." According to this speech, Andrew Butler's chosen mistress was in fact "the harlot, Slavery." Butler's cousin, infuriated by the supposedly libelous content of this speech, beat its author over the head with a gutta-percha cane. For 10 points, Preston Brooks attacked Charles Sumner for delivering what 1856 speech about the violence of the "slave power" in a western frontier territory?

French territories in this ocean include an island with capital Saint-Denis [sahn deh-NEE], R´eunion. Near the Laccadive Sea, Adam's Bridge connects an island in this ocean to the mainland. The Nicobar and Andaman Islands are in this ocean, which was rocked by a 2004 tsunami that killed hundreds of thousands of people after an earthquake struck off the coast of Sumatra. The Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea are northern arms of, for 10 points, what ocean between Australia and Africa?

A half-brother of this figure won at the Panathenian Games before being murdered out of jealousy; that half-brother was Androgeus. This figure was conceived after an animal from Poseidon was not sacrificed as promised and seduced by a queen inside a wooden cow. That wooden cow was built by the designer of this creature's enclosure. Also known as Asterion, this beast received seven sacrifices every year from Athens. This creature's half-sister, Ariadne, gave a ball of string to Theseus which allowed Theseus to navigate out of the Labyrinth after killing this creature. For 10 points, name this Greek creature with the body of a man and the head of a bull.

Philon of Byblos's account of Phoenician mythology identifies this deity with El and claims that he was the father of Persephone and Athena. Homer and Hesiod often call this deity "ankulometes," or crooked-minded. The Romans depicted this deity as the consort of either Lua Mater or Ops and as the father of Picus, the first king of Latium. This god's mother created "grey adamant" for this god's best-known task, which resulted in the birth of figures like the Erinyes. This god's wife tricked him into swallowing the omphalos stone, allowing his youngest son to overthrow him and force him to regurgitate the other Olympian gods. For 10 points, name this father of Zeus and leader of the Titans, whom the Romans called Saturn.

A sculptor from this movement used materials like mahogany and painted cement to create 3D models of mathematical equations. Another artist from this movement was inspired by the ultra realistic sketches he made for a North African mining company to create his Mine Triptych. The principles of "Elementarism" inspired another artist from this movement to create his series of Counter-Compositions. Architectural works from this movement include JJP Oud's Municipal Housing Project and Garret Rietveld's Schroder House. This movement's best-known painter limited himself to primary colors and right angles in works like Broadway Boogie Woogie. For 10 points, name this Dutch art movement co-founded by Theo van Doesburg and Piet Mondrian.

Darwin predicted the existence of a Madagascar moth after observing one of these structures, which have separate male/female types in dioecious [dy-oh-EE-shus] species. The parts of this occur in multiples of three in monocots and many use nectar to attract pollinators. One mature part of this becomes the fruit, and it has stamen and carpel reproductive organs. For 10 points, name this structure found in angiosperm plants, often surrounded by petals.

Francesco Salviati was hanged at this city's town hall, the Palazzo Vecchio, after Giuliano, the son of Piero the Gouty, was killed in this city's cathedral, the Duomo. That Pazzi Conspiracy sought to assassinate Lorenzo the Magnificent to take over this capital of Tuscany. Pisa and Milan were rivals of, for 10 points, what Italian city, ruled by the Medici family during the Renaissance?

parts.text: This scientist who co-names a statistical distribution with Dirac designed the first reactor to achieve self-sustaining nuclear fusion, Chicago Pile-1. He also names a set of particles that includes electrons and muons.

Fermi's golden rule is used to calculate transition rates in this branch of physics. This branch of physics uses Schroedinger's equation to calculate the wavefunction of systems like the particle-in-a-box.
Quantum mechanics predicts this result in which a particle goes through a potential barrier that it could not escape classically. Gamow explained alpha decay by using this process.

bonuses.leadin: In a transcript from the American Society of Physics' oral histories, Werner Heisenberg talks at length about the effect of this scientist's 1934 paper on beta decay. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 18th century economic policy in which a nation tried to maximize the amount of gold and silver it possessed.
This Scottish economist was a vicious opponent of mercantilism, attacking it in works like The Theory of Moral Sentiments and The Wealth of Nations.

Smith's theories were inspired by the Physiocrats, who argued that this activity was the primary driver of economic success. Franc¸ois Quesnay [kay-nay] divided the economy into the "sterile" class of merchants, the "proprietary" class of landowners, and the "productive" class, who provide this kind of labor to the landowners.

bonuses.leadin: This theory often led to high tariffs, monopolies, economic wars, and a devotion to keeping a trade surplus out of fears of enriching other countries. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this play about Nina Zarachnaya's becoming an actress to learn to endure, and about the suicide of Konstantin Treplev, who puts on a dream-play starring Nina.
In addition to the stories "The Steppe," "The Duel," and "Ward No. 6," this author wrote such plays as The Seagull and Uncle Vanya.

Called "Russia's only hope" by his lover Irina Arkadina, mother of Konstantin, this writer is loved by Nina, who leaves home for him in Moscow. But when he grew tired of Nina after she gave birth, she turned to prostitution.

bonuses.leadin: Sorin wants to write a book called "The Man Who Wanted," about having an urge to get married and to write, but accomplishing neither. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with complement system.
What is the main function of the phagocyte in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to complement system.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Identify this NBC TV series in which Zachary Levi stars as the titular Buy More employee protected by NSA agents Sarah Walker and John Casey.
This fellow Buy More employee is Chuck's best friend. He has an on-again off-again relationship with Anna Wu and eventually quits his job to become a chef in Hawaii.
The 2nd season saw the introduction of the criminal mastermind Ted Roark, played by this actor. More notable roles include Ty Webb in Caddyshack and Clark Griswold in the Vacation films.

bonuses.leadin: The titular character of this series got kicked out of Stanford for cheating based on the false accusations of Bryce Larkin, who was responsible for sending that character the Intersect. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Kalidasa play in which Dushyanta is cursed by the sage Durvasa into forgetting the title character.

Kalidasa also wrote Vikramorvasiyam, a play in which Pururvava falls in love with this Apsara woman. She writes a love letter on a birch leaf and is is banished from heaven until her lover sees their child.
The Recognition of Shakuntala and Vikramorvasiyam were based on this Indian epic written by Vyasa. In the Bhagavad Gita section of this work, Krishna calls Arjuna to action.

bonuses.leadin: A signet ring in this work is lost when the title character dips her hand into the water; it is then eaten by a fish. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Hasidism was founded by this rabbi in what is today Western Ukraine. He believed that the worship of God involved finding direct attachment to God, called dvekut, in prayer throughout daily life.

Hasidism includes elements of this school of Jewish mysticism whose foundational text, the Zohar, suggests reading the Torah on four levels given the acronym pardes. It aims to connect the mortal world with an infinite god.
Most American Hasidic Jews reside in this US city, also the city home to the most Jews in the world.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following questions about Hasidic Judaism, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this play in which the anarchist Jack Tanner becomes the guardian of a woman referred to as the "Life Force," Ann Whitefield.
This author of Man and Superman described Eliza Doolittle's transformation from a flower girl into a society lady in his play Pygmalion.

The third act of Man and Superman features the actor who plays Jack Tanner also playing this character talking to the Devil. That act is occasionally produced as a separate work titled [this character] in Hell.

bonuses.leadin: A character in this play is the author of "The Revolutionist's Handbook and Pocket Companion." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this precursor to the laser, which emits microwaves instead of a laser's visible light.
acceptableAnswers: microwave amplification by stimulated emission of radiation

parts.text: MASERS, like lasers, rely on the gain medium achieving this state, in which a greater fraction of atoms are in an excited state than the ground state.
Both lasers and MASERs operate by emitting coherent beams of these quanta of light. The energy of these particles equals Planck's ("plonkʼs") constant times their frequency.

bonuses.leadin: Charles Townes invented the first of these devices, which used ammonia as a medium. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this orchestral work whose original composer died before completing its third movement.
acceptableAnswers: accept Franz Schubert’s Symphony No. 8 in B minor

parts.text: The Unfinished Symphony was written by this composer of Winterreise. He also wrote the lied ("LEED") Gretchen at the Spinning Wheel as well as the Trout Quintet.
Schubert also composed eight of these solo piano pieces one year prior to his death. Chopin composed a "Fantaisie" one of these in 1834.

bonuses.leadin: August Ludwig added a "Philosopher's Scherzo" and "March of Destiny" to the end of this work. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Also known as the multiplicative inverse, give this term which, for a non-zero real number n, equates to one over n.
This type of mean for n variables is equal to n divided by the sum of the variables' reciprocals.
In studying infinite series, the harmonic series is the sum, from n equals one to n equals infinity, of the fraction one over n. That series notably has this behavior, contrasted with convergence.

bonuses.leadin: This value for the golden ratio is exactly one less than the golden ratio itself. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this term from anthropology used to describe subjective accounts, usually given by someone within a culture. It is often contrasted with the outsider perspective or "etic".
The terms "emic" and "etic" were popularized by Marvin Harris, who was a professor at this university. This university had the first PhD-granting department of anthropology in the United States.
This man, who studied the Kwakiutl, founded the department of anthropology at Columbia. He argued against racist ideas of intelligence in his The Mind of Primitive Man.

bonuses.leadin: Kenneth Pike originally developed this term and its counterpart to describe linguistic behaviors. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with feedback loops.
What is the main function of the hypothalamus in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to feedback loops.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Those two parties were opposing parties in this Scandinavian country. Under Sigurd I, they went on their namesake crusade and captured Sidon before going back home. Its leader Harald Hardrada invaded England.

The civil war between the Birkebeiners and Baglers was ended with the ascension of this king, medieval Norway's greatest. During his youth he was brought to safety by birkebeiner skiers and he later invaded Scotland.

The Baglers were named after the crosiers of these clergy, who naturally supported them. The Popes are said to be successor of Peter who is often said to be the first one to hold this position in Rome.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name some things regarding your favorite opposing parties, the Birkebeiners and Baglers.

parts.text: Joining the Ligurian Alps at their north, this mountain range stretches the entire length of the Italian peninsula.
This range, whose highest peak is the Pico del Aneto, serves as a natural border between Spain and France.
The Tatra Mountains, which serve as the natural border between Poland and Slovakia, are the highest sub range of this mountain range which runs through Central and Southern Europe.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these European mountain ranges for 10 points each.

parts.text: Identify this Hindu god of thunder and war who drinks soma and leads the Aryan conquest of India.
Indra appears in 250 hymns as the highest god in this ancient text. This text is the oldest of the four Sanskrit texts composed around the 2nd to 1st millenium BC.
Indra is often depicted riding Airavata, this type of creature. A god with the head of this creature is often depicted riding a mouse.

bonuses.leadin: After Hanuman mistook the Sun for a fruit and tried to swallow it, this god struck him with his thunderbolt. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this king. The Geste de Doon de Mayence deals with rebellions against this ruler, who is served by paladins like Roland.
This warrior, who wields the sword Cortana, originally fights against Charlemagne but then joins his court. This Danish warrior eventually moves to Avalon with the fairy Morgana.

After killing Charlemagne's nephew, the four sons of Aymon flee with this horse, who can adjust his size to match his riders. This horse smashes a stone around his neck and escapes when Charlemagne tries to drown him.

bonuses.leadin: To atone for unknowingly killing this ruler's son, Huon de Bordeaux is given impossible tasks like kissing the daughter of the emir of Babylon four times. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this section of a musical triptych named after its basis, a collection of 13th century poems.
In addition to Catulli Carmina and Trionfo di Afrodite, this German composer of the musical settings Die Kluge and Antigone wrote Carmina Burana.
This opera by Orff was finished in 1972, ten years before his death. Containing the "Venio ad Te" it also sees a viola quartet as it presents a mystery play.

bonuses.leadin: Its thirteen movements are split into five sections, including "Blanziflor et Helena" and "Primo Vere," and it opens and closes with the "O Fortuna" chorus. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this lightest alkali metal which, along with Strontium, has a red flame test. It has atomic number 3 and the symbol Li.

The winner of the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, Dr John Goodenough, used lithium ions to develop a rechargeable type of these devices; previous designs used the "nickel-cadmium" type of these devices.

A "pile" named after this man is often considered to be the first functional battery. He is also known for the isolation of methane, as well as for naming the SI unit of electric potential difference.

bonuses.leadin: Salts of this element are sometimes used to treat bipolar disorder. For 10 points each:

parts.text: At the behest of the FBI, this city's police department drugged young black activist Fred Hampton and shot him 99 times in his sleep. More recently, this city's police department has come under fire for running an extrajudicial "black site" at Homan Square.

The Chicago Police Department falsely claimed to the media that Hampton had been killed during a chaotic gunfight with members of this civil rights activist organization named for a type of wild cat. No such gunfight occurred.
The FBI also sent this man a blackmail letter demanding that he commit suicide. This man delivered the "I Have a Dream" speech during the March on Washington.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the attempted and successful killings of civil rights activists by the US government:
